newsitem.title: FRANCE: Corsican petrol stations close in protest.
newsitem.headline: Corsican petrol stations close in protest.

text.p: All 180 petrol stations on the French Mediterranean island of Corsica stayed closed on Friday in protest at the blocking by farmers of the island's two petrol depots, officials said.
The farmers blocked the depots at Bastia and Ajaccio on Tuesday to press their demands on the government for a re-scheduling of debts and other issues.
The petrol station owners association said they were closing their stations because they had "had enough of being taken hostage" each time there was a social problem on the island.
The stations were already forced to close for several days in December when a lorry-drivers' strike blocked roads and prevented supplies from reaching them.
The petrol station owners apparently expect public pressure for their product to mount quickly and to incite the government to force farmers to abandon their blockade on the depots.
The farmers' action was apparently unconnected to tensions cause by a government crackdown on Corsican separatists seeking more autonomy from France.
